A8_counterexample.violation: A8 says coarse L should force refined L on [L,M], but midpoint rule returns M because 19/4>9/2.

midpoint_theorem.nontrivial_axioms: A3 pins the symmetry center, A5 removes reflection-symmetric oscillatory selectors, and A4 forbids a wider unresolved interval away from the fixed point. A0 supplies legal endpoint typing.
midpoint_theorem.proof_left: For q<m=(L+U)/2, if S(q)=U then monotonicity gives S(J(q))=U because J(q)>q; reflection equivariance requires S(J(q))=L, contradiction. Hence S(q)=L.
midpoint_theorem.proof_midpoint: J(m)=m and endpoint reflection swaps L,U, so no singleton endpoint is fixed; the exact equivariant value is unresolved {L,U}.
midpoint_theorem.proof_right: Apply reflection to the left-side result: q>m implies S(q)=U.

normalization: Under A1+A2 a generic interval selector can be represented by t=(q-L)/(U-L), but the midpoint theorem itself only needs the within-gap ordered/reflection axioms listed below.

package_results.counterclass: arbitrary legal branch assignment; q=5 may map to 4 or 9
any normalized threshold alpha in (0,1) is translation/positive-scale covariant; q=5 has t=1/5 and may lie on either side depending alpha
choose any Boolean pattern on 0<t<1/2 and define s(1-t)=1-s(t); exact midpoint remains unresolved. Reflection alone permits multiple switches.
monotone threshold alpha is arbitrary without reflection equivariance.

package_results.selector: same midpoint rule plus translation/positive-scale covariance and endpoint idempotence

package_results.reason: A3+A4+A5 already force midpoint rule, but declared A8 one-sided refinement control is violated by that rule; thus A8 is rejected as an overstrong compatibility candidate, not used to derive midpoint.

scalar_5.P_MONOTONE: {4,9} both admissible across monotone threshold family
scalar_5.interpretation: 5->4 is derived only conditional on explicit reflection+determinism+order-monotonicity package; it is not a theorem of completion-neighbor legality alone.
